original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture, and test a Server in Space (SiS) module for regenerative processors in satellite communication systems, enablingefficienton-board data processing and offering advanced autonomy applications andemergency management services.TargetedImprovements: Enabling application layer processing on-board for Servers in Space to offer advanced autonomy applications and emergency management services.Description: It is expected that satellites will have a larger percentage of regenerative processing, which opens the door to application layer processing on-board of satellites. The mainchallenge to be addressed is the availability of a Server in Space (SiS) with application layer processing, with technical challenges to be addressed in terms of powerconsumption, radiation hardening of ground-based data centre technology, and maturity of application layersoftware for embedded devices. Additionally, aspects of modularityand scalability for larger space datacentres shall be considered. Recent advancements of cloud providers in embedded processors, as well as technical developments inefficient FPGAs and computational memories, allow to link this concept to 5G/6G Non-Terrestrial-Networks (NTN) and Direct-to-Device (D2D) connectivity, enabling thesatellite to act as a server in space. By integrating the application layer on the satellite, cloud services, currently only provided on ground, could be made available to users innatural disaster situations or with special requirements that cannot use the regular network, e.g. very stringent latency needs like Internet-of-Things (IoT) or autonomousdriving.This activity will design and develop a cloud computing module, integrate it with the regenerative processor, and test it to ensure its efficiency and reliability inthe relevantenvironment. Focus shall be on the interfaces between the payload and components in the module, including also technologies used on ground, due to the high data ratesrequired. A fully functional Server in Space (SiS) module engineering module, capable of efficient on-board data processing and data storage, shall be designed, developedand tested. The SiS module shall demonstrateits capability to be integrated in future satcom digital processors and to be scaled to large data centres in space.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

Additionally, aspects of modularityand scalability for larger space datacentres shall be considered. Recent advancements of cloud providers in embedded processors, as well as technical developments inefficient FPGAs and computational memories, allow to link this concept to 5G/6G Non-Terrestrial-Networks (NTN) and Direct-to-Device (D2D) connectivity, enabling thesatellite to act as a server in space. By integrating the application layer on the satellite, cloud services, currently only provided on ground, could be made available to users innatural disaster situations or with special requirements that cannot use the regular network, e.g. very stringent latency needs like Internet-of-Things (IoT) or autonomousdriving.This activity will design and develop a cloud computing module, integrate it with the regenerative processor, and test it to ensure its efficiency and reliability inthe relevantenvironment. Focus shall be on the interfaces between the payload and components in the module, including also technologies used on ground, due to the high data ratesrequired. A fully functional Server in Space (SiS) module engineering module, capable of efficient on-board data processing and data storage, shall be designed, developedand tested. The SiS module shall demonstrateits capability to be integrated in future satcom digital processors and to be scaled to large data centres in space.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. original.description: The increase in small satellite missions has intensified the need for compliance to international space debris de-orbiting requirements. To meet these requirements CubeSat-class missions frequently rely on their primary On-Board Computer (OBC) and Electrical Power Subsystem (EPS) to activate disposal mechanisms, however deployment and late-mission failures; such as battery degradation, bus freeze, or cyber compromise; can prevent successful disposal execution.This activity addresses this gap through the development of the Secure Autonomous Disposal Interface and Safety Module: a standardised, independent Disposal Trigger Module (DTM) compatible withCubeSat buses from 1U to 16U across a variety of disposal mechanisms. The DTM shall implement two autonomy levels of increasing complexity and prove resilient to spacecraft failures and cyberattacks. The project targets bring the technology to TRL6.

original.description: Objective of the activity is to develop and test positioning-independent techniques for Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) air interfaces.Targeted Improvements:Enable positioning independency for ground NTN terminals.Description: The development of a positioning-independent air-interface is deemed essential for future 6G NTN. Conventional 5G NTN terminals rely heavily on GNSS for positioning andtiming information, which means a terminal with no or poor GNSS reception cannot use NTN technology. Moreover, GNSS signals are vulnerable to spoofing and jamming,which can compromise the reliability and security of the communication links. By developing positioning-independent techniques, NTN terminals can operate without relying onGNSS or other positioning systems / sensors, enabling indoor coverage which is one of the goals in 6G for NTN as defined in the 3GPP roadmap. This feature is also crucialfor maintaining reliable communication in various scenarios, including critical infrastructure and emergency response. Positioning-independent modems can then operate inenvironments where positioning signals are weak or unavailable, such as indoors, urban canyons, or remote areas. This flexibility enhances the overall coverage and reliabilityof NTN services.This activity will explore the use of alternative techniques and protocols enabling a positioning-independent NTN air interface. Techniques and protocols shall be implementedin a modem prototype and evaluated in a real-time testbed possibly based on open radio stack.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). original.description: In-Orbit Servicing Assembly  Manufacturing is a cornerstone of the ESA Strategy 2040, and the capability to perform the refurbishment and upgrade of assets in orbit will pave the way for a myriad of new possible life-extension services and enable circularity in the use of the assets in orbit. As a result, ESA has identified refurbishment as its primary near-term goal for the next generation of in-orbit servicing missions.This activity will further mature the concept of the ORUM missions with competitive contracts for Phase A2. The result of the activity and the maturation of the ORUM concept should lay the groundwork for a Phase B1 and System Requirements Review in later activities.

original.description: ObjectivesTo develop a low frequency and low noise, 3 axis electric field probe, enabling direct ongroundverification by test fornext generation in-situ space plasma sensing missions and for missions with EMC sensitive payload integrated inside the spacecraft structure.DescriptionBackground and Context:Missions that are studying space plasma with wave instruments are imposing low frequency and low-level electric field requirements on the spacecraft in order to limit the unwanted radiated emission that could disturbthe instrument performance. In addition, other increasingly challenging and sensitive payloads also require more stringent control ofelectric fields at lower frequencies. Therefore, the on-ground verification of the electric field requirements driven by the payloads has paramount importance i.e. to confirm the presence of unintentional electric field interference originated from the spacecraftthat can jeopardize the instrument performance. Current electric field probes do not cover the needs of compact probing of low frequency and low noise radiated electric fields in which 3 axes and phase information is needed, in particular to characterise emissions close to units or even inside the spacecraft. By improving both the frequency range and thesensitivity, compact electric field probes could be utilised for improved verification and new applications that were not feasible before.Justification:The commercially available electric field probes are not suitable to capture the low frequencies and the low amplitudes, that are required for upcoming missions of Plasma Observatory, M-Matisse and New ATHENA or required by already flying missions like JUICE and Solar Orbiter.Description:The goal of the activity is to develop a triaxial field probe together with its conditioning unit with start frequency of 0.1 Hz or lower and sensitivity of 0.5 mV/m or lower up-to 200 kHz.An additional constraint for the field probe development is the size. The newly developed field probe shall allow to place minimum of 16 identical field probes around the unit under test at a distance closer than 0.25 m without interfering with each other.Moreover, the field probe needs to produce the field data along eachprincipal axes that can be processed with typical laboratory equipment like spectrum analyser, EMI receiver, digital oscilloscope, data acquisition unit, etc.Task list:- Identification of technology concepts and market research for state-of-the-art field probes in terms of frequency range, sensitivity and dynamic range- Evaluation of weak points of the existing field probes and identification of the critical components needed for the required improvements- Bread boarding of 3 axis sensor (e.g. optimize the type, sizeand shape of sensor) together with its conditioning unit (e.g. design a low noise read out chain including low noise amplifier) also considering constraints like size and cost- Validation tests and reportsDeliverables:- Documentation of the research- The bread board of the improved field probe together with its conditioning unit- Test reports and calibration data

Current electric field probes do not cover the needs of compact probing of low frequency and low noise radiated electric fields in which 3 axes and phase information is needed, in particular to characterise emissions close to units or even inside the spacecraft. By improving both the frequency range and thesensitivity, compact electric field probes could be utilised for improved verification and new applications that were not feasible before.Justification:The commercially available electric field probes are not suitable to capture the low frequencies and the low amplitudes, that are required for upcoming missions of Plasma Observatory, M-Matisse and New ATHENA or required by already flying missions like JUICE and Solar Orbiter.Description:The goal of the activity is to develop a triaxial field probe together with its conditioning unit with start frequency of 0.1 Hz or lower and sensitivity of 0.5 mV/m or lower up-to 200 kHz.An additional constraint for the field probe development is the size. The newly developed field probe shall allow to place minimum of 16 identical field probes around the unit under test at a distance closer than 0.25 m without interfering with each other.Moreover, the field probe needs to produce the field data along eachprincipal axes that can be processed with typical laboratory equipment like spectrum analyser, EMI receiver, digital oscilloscope, data acquisition unit, etc.Task list:- Identification of technology concepts and market research for state-of-the-art field probes in terms of frequency range, sensitivity and dynamic range- Evaluation of weak points of the existing field probes and identification of the critical components needed for the required improvements- Bread boarding of 3 axis sensor (e.g. optimize the type, sizeand shape of sensor) together with its conditioning unit (e.g. design a low noise read out chain including low noise amplifier) also considering constraints like size and cost- Validation tests and reportsDeliverables:- Documentation of the research- The bread board of the improved field probe together with its conditioning unit- Test reports and calibration data
